cue: The sharpest part is a band along the horizon. Tap the screen to move the focus.

DEUTAN.note: Vienot, Brettel and Mollon 1999, entered from memory

rows: Dogs see about a quarter to a seventh as much detail as people do. This view is blurred to match.
Dogs with long noses see most sharply along a band level with the horizon. Dogs with short noses see most sharply in one central spot. This view shows the band.
Dogs have two kinds of colour-sensing cells, where people have three. This view shows colours as a person with two kinds would see them.
Field of view, dim light and depth
These parts of the view are guesses. This view treats things lower in the picture as closer.
